records.text: Donald Trump, Kash Patel, and Pam Bondi intentionally covered up for Jared Kushner's Israeli business friends, the Alexander brothers, who sold Ivanka Trump and Jared Kushner their Miami mansion and were found guilty of sex trafficking.
records.speaker: Candace Owens

appearances.snippet: At the very least, we can now assert that they intentionally covered up for Jared Kushner's Israeli business friends who sold Ivanka and Jared (Jared Kushner) their Miami mansion and they were just found guilty of sex trafficking.

verification.notes: The Alexander brothers were convicted of federal sex offenses, and Oren Alexander represented Ivanka Trump and Jared Kushner as buyers of a Miami property. The property was not sold by the brothers, and current sources do not establish that Trump, Patel, or Bondi intentionally protected them because of a Kushner relationship.

records.text: Kash Patel said the Epstein files contained no evidence of trafficking, even though Tal, Oren, and Alon Alexander appeared in the files.
records.speaker: Candace Owens

appearances.snippet: Remember, Kash Patel said there was no evidence of trafficking in the files. None. Yet these Israeli-American brothers, Tal, Oren, and Alon Alexander, were indeed in the files.

verification.notes: Patel testified that the FBI had no credible information that Epstein trafficked victims to other individuals, while expressly adding that he was not saying others were not involved. The Alexander brothers' names later appeared in released material, but reporting says they were not accused of involvement in Epstein's abuse. The extracted statement overstates Patel and conflates unrelated records.

records.text: The Alexander brothers visited the White House multiple times, attended its annual Hanukkah party, and had their last names redacted from the Epstein files.
records.speaker: Candace Owens

appearances.snippet: They certainly visited the White House multiple times. They even were invited to the annual Hanukkah party. And I'm wondering if it's because of that that they had their last names redacted from the Epstein files.

verification.notes: Oren and Alon Alexander attended the 2020 White House Hanukkah party, and the brothers' names appeared in later Epstein-related releases. Available reliable sources did not establish multiple White House visits by all three or clearly confirm that their surname was intentionally redacted as claimed.

records.text: A jury found Tal, Oren, and Alon Alexander guilty of all ten federal counts against them.
records.speaker: Tom Hanson

appearances.snippet: More than a year after the Alexander brothers were first arrested on charges including sex trafficking, a jury found the trio guilty of all 10 counts against them Monday.

verification.notes: CBS and federal reporting confirm that a Manhattan jury convicted Tal, Oren, and Alon Alexander on every count they faced; CBS described the verdict as guilty on all ten counts.

records.text: The Trump administration used Epstein-file redactions to protect rapists and sex traffickers because they donated to the Israel Defense Forces.
records.speaker: Candace Owens

appearances.snippet: What's going on here is they have just proven they were willing to lie via redactions to the American people to protect rapists, Israeli rapists, and sex traffickers because they donate to the IDF.

verification.notes: Oren Alexander publicly organized fundraising for Friends of the IDF and improper Epstein-file redactions are documented, but no reliable source establishes that the administration redacted records to protect the Alexanders because of those activities. Motive and intent remain unproven.
